thread:
maria: Quick sync — we need to pick an upgrade strategy for the Private deploy fleet (VPC/on‑prem) we ship to customers in Q2. Two fast options in play: forklift (big switch, short per-tenant downtime) vs phased (compat layer/operator shim, near-zero downtime but longer calendar).
kevin: Forklift = simpler runtime delta, smaller surface area to test. Rollback is hairy though. dev estimate: ~3 sprints + 1 test sprint.
sam: Field perspective: high-touch customers with strict maintenance windows hate big switches. We can carve maintenance windows but it delays momentum.
anya: Netops: phased aligns with customers that have change freeze windows. But phased needs strong compatibility tests and dual-run networking (two stacks) which increases infra cost during rollout.
liz: Installer UX note: whichever path we pick we must expose progress + clear rollback messaging. For phased we need a migration status API so NetOps can monitor.
maria: TL;DR: forklift = faster to deliver but higher short-term risk and support burden. phased = more work but safer for enterprise. Proposing decision criteria: customer risk profile, install size (#nodes/tenants), SLO for downtime, support runway.
kevin: Can we do a hybrid? e.g., forklift for small tenants (<20 nodes) and phased for large ones. That would reduce scope and let us validate.
sam: Hybrid is the pragmatic choice. We already have some scripts that can convert configs; migrating state should be doable in ~20-30m for many customers if we orchestrate.
maria: +1 hybrid. Need acceptance gates: automated canary on staging, a 2-week limited field pilot, and a rollback playbook. Also need to quantify support hours.
anya: Also callout: VPN/peering churn during forklift is the biggest failure mode we've seen. For hybrid we should require a preflight network sanity check: `net-check --tenant $TENANT`.
kevin: For phased we need an operator shim + dual-kv support in runtime. Rough sketch: implement compatibility layer that translates old handshake -> new handshake, route by header. Estimate: 6 weeks core + 3 weeks tests.
liz: UX for hybrid: add a "migration mode" flag in console with per-tenant timeline and manual override.
maria: I'll write up an RFC with the hybrid proposal and acceptance gates. Draft milestones I want feedback on: 
- M0 (2w): decision + partner customer list
- M1 (4w): canary tooling + preflight checks + migration scripts
- M2 (6w): operator shim POC + console migration UI
- M3 (10w): limited field pilot (3 customers), rollback docs, runbook
- M4 (14w): ramp to general customers
kevin: dev ask: freeze breaking infra changes for M1 -> give us time to land the shim.
sam: field ask: pick 3 pilot customers representing small/med/large and lock them in. I'll reach out to get buy-in.
anya: ops ask: reserve temporary capacity for dual-run during pilot (estimate +30% GPUs for 2 weeks).
deploy-bot: Deploy CI: canary job queued: `canary-run/private-migration/PILOT-001` — status: queued.
maria: Action items: kevin — dev plan + rollback checklist by EOD Fri; sam — pilot customer confirmations by Mon; anya — capacity reservation by Mon; liz — console mockups by Tue. If no objections I'll schedule the decision sync on Wed 10am.
liz: noted, will share mocks in #design tomorrow.
kevin: no objections. leaning hybrid.
sam: +1 hybrid.
maria: Okay locking hybrid as direction for RFC. Thanks all.
